q: Which IPC section deals with Murder?
explain: IPC Section 302 prescribes punishment for murder — death penalty or life imprisonment plus fine.

q: What is the unified emergency helpline number in India?
explain: 112 is India's unified emergency number launched in 2018 — connects police, fire and ambulance.

q: Under which Act is cybercrime punishable in India?
explain: The Information Technology Act 2000 (Section 66) governs cybercrimes. Report at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930.

q: What should you do FIRST after witnessing a crime?
explain: Always call emergency services first. Your safety matters most.

q: Which helpline number is for women in distress?
explain: 1091 is India's dedicated Women Helpline available 24x7.

q: IPC Section 420 deals with which crime?
explain: IPC 420 covers cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property. Up to 7 years imprisonment.

q: What does FIR stand for?
explain: FIR — First Information Report — is the document filed with police to report a cognizable offence. It is your legal right to file one free of cost.

q: Child helpline number in India is?
explain: 1098 is Childline India — a 24-hour free helpline for children in distress.

q: Which IPC section covers Kidnapping?
explain: IPC Section 363 deals with kidnapping. Punishment is imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.

q: Can police refuse to register an FIR for a cognizable offence?
options: Yes, if the crime is small
No, it is your legal right
explain: Police CANNOT legally refuse to register an FIR for a cognizable offence. If refused, approach the Superintendent of Police or a Judicial Magistrate.

q: IPC Section 498A deals with which offence?
explain: IPC 498A covers cruelty by husband or his relatives towards a wife. It is cognizable and non-bailable. Punishment is up to 3 years + fine.

q: Under POCSO Act, the minimum age of a child is?
explain: POCSO (Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012) defines a child as any person below 18 years of age.

q: What is the RTI application fee?
explain: The RTI application fee is Rs. 10 (BPL applicants are exempt). It can be paid via IPO, DD, or online.

q: Within how many days must a PIO respond to an RTI application?
explain: Under Section 7(1) of RTI Act, the Public Information Officer must respond within 30 days. For life/liberty matters, it is 48 hours.

q: Which section of IPC covers rape?
explain: IPC Section 376 prescribes punishment for rape — minimum 10 years to life imprisonment. Section 375 defines rape.

q: IT Act Section 66C deals with?
explain: IT Act Section 66C covers identity theft — fraudulently using another's password or signature. Punishment is up to 3 years + Rs.1 lakh fine.

q: Under CrPC, within how many hours must an arrested person be produced before a magistrate?
explain: Under Section 57 of CrPC (now BNSS Section 35), an arrested person must be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours of arrest, excluding travel time.

q: What is 'cognizable offence'?
options: Offence where police cannot arrest without warrant
Offence where police can arrest without warrant
Offence only tried in High Court
explain: A cognizable offence is one where police can arrest without a warrant, register FIR, and begin investigation without magistrate's permission. Murder, rape, robbery are cognizable.

q: Section 354A of IPC covers?
explain: IPC 354A covers sexual harassment including unwelcome physical contact, sexual overtures, or demand for sexual favours. Punishment is up to 3 years.

q: Under POCSO Act, who is mandated to report child sexual abuse?
options: Any person who has knowledge of the offence
explain: POCSO Section 19 mandates that ANY person who has knowledge of a sexual offence against a child MUST report it to the police or SJPU. Failure to report is an offence.

q: What is bail?
options: Temporary release from custody on condition
explain: Bail is a temporary release from custody subject to conditions, including a surety bond. It is a right for bailable offences and discretionary for non-bailable ones.

q: IT Act Section 67B covers?
explain: IT Act Section 67B specifically punishes publishing or transmitting child sexually explicit material online. Punishment is up to 7 years + fine.

q: Which Act governs domestic violence cases in India?
explain: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 provides civil remedies including Protection Orders, Residence Orders, and monetary relief for victims.

q: IPC Section 307 deals with?
explain: IPC 307 covers attempt to commit murder. Punishment is up to 10 years, and if hurt is caused, it can extend to life imprisonment.

q: Under RTI Act, who can file an RTI application?
explain: Only Indian citizens can file RTI applications. Non-citizens, companies, and NGOs (unless filed by a citizen on their behalf) are not eligible.

q: What is 'phishing' under IT Act?
options: Fraudulent attempt to steal credentials online
explain: Phishing is a cyber fraud where criminals impersonate legitimate organisations to trick victims into sharing passwords or financial info. Punishable under IT Act Sections 66, 66C, 66D.

q: IPC Section 354D covers?
explain: IPC Section 354D covers stalking — repeatedly following, contacting, or monitoring a woman against her will. 1st offence: 3 years. Repeat: 5 years.

q: Under NDPS Act, what is 'small quantity' for cannabis?
explain: Under NDPS Act, small quantity for cannabis (ganja) is up to 500 grams and for hashish is 100 grams. Small quantity attracts lesser punishment — up to 1 year.

q: Which section of BNSS 2023 (replacing CrPC) covers FIR registration?
explain: Section 154 of CrPC (now BNSS Section 173) mandates FIR registration. The Supreme Court in Lalita Kumari vs UP mandated that FIR MUST be registered for cognizable offences.

q: What is a 'deepfake' and is it covered under Indian law?
options: Real video of crime — not covered
AI-manipulated video — covered under IT Act
explain: Deepfakes are AI-generated manipulated videos. They can attract IT Act sections 66E (privacy violation), 67 (obscene content), and IPC 499/500 (defamation) depending on content and intent.

q: Under IPC 406, which crime is punishable?
explain: IPC 406 covers criminal breach of trust — when someone entrusted with property dishonestly misappropriates it. Punishment is up to 3 years or fine or both.

q: What does 'compoundable offence' mean?
options: Offence that can be settled between parties
explain: Compoundable offences (under IPC Section 320) can be settled between the complainant and accused, often without court intervention. Examples: assault, defamation. Murder is non-compoundable.

q: Which court has jurisdiction for serious offences like murder and rape?
explain: The Sessions Court (District and Sessions Court) has original jurisdiction for serious IPC offences including murder (302), rape (376), and dacoity (395). The HC and SC are appellate courts.

q: Mandatory reporting under POCSO must be made to whom?
options: Police or Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU)
explain: Under POCSO Section 19, any person with knowledge of an offence must report it to the local police or Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) immediately.

q: What is the first appeal process under RTI Act?
options: Appeal to the Appellate Authority within 30 days
explain: Under RTI Section 19(1), if not satisfied with PIO response, file 1st appeal to the Appellate Authority (senior officer) within 30 days. 2nd appeal goes to CIC/SIC within 90 days.

q: IT Act 66F covers?
explain: IT Act Section 66F covers cyber terrorism — attacks on critical infrastructure, government systems, or computer networks that threaten national security. Punishment is life imprisonment.

q: Under IPC Section 304B, what is the minimum punishment for Dowry Death?
explain: IPC Section 304B (Dowry Death) carries a MINIMUM 7 years imprisonment. If a woman dies within 7 years of marriage due to burns/injuries connected to dowry demands, IPC 304B applies.

q: What should you do if police refuse to register your FIR?
explain: If police refuse FIR registration for a cognizable offence, you can: (1) Send FIR by registered post to SP, (2) File complaint before Magistrate under CrPC Section 156(3), (3) File Writ in High Court.

q: Under which Act are zero FIR provisions mandated?
explain: Zero FIR allows filing an FIR at ANY police station regardless of jurisdiction. The BNSS 2023 (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita) has codified Zero FIR provisions.

q: What is the Cyber Crime national reporting portal?
explain: cybercrime.gov.in is India's official online portal for reporting cybercrime complaints. You can also call 1930 for cyber crime helpline support.
